pl-l3d28c1-d1e115.summary: Asks whether the commandment to love the neighbor commands us to love the whole neighbor, soul and body, and our whole selves.

pl-l3d28c1-d1e118.summary: Answers that every kind of thing to be loved is contained in the two commandments.
claims: The two commandments contain every kind of thing to be loved.

pl-l3d28c1-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: there are four things to be loved, God above us, ourselves, neighbor beside us, and our body below us. No commandments needed to be given about the second and fourth, since however far a man falls from truth, love of himself and his body remains; no one ever hated his own flesh, and the just who chastise the body hate its corruption and weight, not the body.
claims: There are four objects of love.
Self-love and love of one's body need no commandment because they remain naturally.

pl-l3d28c1-d1e140.summary: Raises a difficulty: Augustine seems to say that we are not bound by commandment to love ourselves or our body. If so, not every kind of thing to be loved is contained in the two commandments, though we ought to love ourselves and our body, which seems to need a commandment, since 'whoever loves iniquity hates his soul'.

pl-l3d28c1-d1e152.summary: Replies that no special commandment needed to be given for self-love or love of the body, since it is contained in 'love your neighbor as yourself', where the whole neighbor and the whole self are to be understood.
claims: Love of the whole self and the whole neighbor is contained in the commandment of love of neighbor.

pl-l3d28c1-d1e158.summary: Confirms with Augustine: if you understand yourself and your neighbor wholly, soul and body, no kind of thing to be loved is left out; love of self, though not stated separately, is not omitted in 'as yourself'. Lombard notes Augustine openly says the commandment contains love of the whole neighbor and the whole self.
claims: The commandment of neighbor-love contains love of the whole self.

pl-l3d28c1-d1e170.summary: Concludes how to understand the claim that no commandments were given about self and body: no special, separate ones, since all is contained in the one, and since we love ourselves and what belongs to us below us by a law of nature found even in beasts. So separate commandments concern God above us and neighbor beside us, and the second contains love of self and body.
claims: No separate commandments are given for self-love and love of the body.
Self-love and love of one's body come by a natural law also present in animals.

pl-l3d28c1.summary: Asks whether the commandment to love the neighbor commands love of the whole neighbor, soul and body, and of our whole selves. Every kind of thing to be loved is contained in the two commandments. Augustine lists four objects of love, God, ourselves, neighbor, and our body, and says no commandments were needed for the second and fourth, since self-love and love of one's body remain in everyone. This seems to say that we are not bound by commandment to love ourselves, which would leave something outside the two commandments. Lombard resolves it from Augustine himself: no special separate commandment is given, since love of the whole self and the whole neighbor is contained in 'love your neighbor as yourself', and we love ourselves and our body by a law of nature found even in beasts.
claims: Every kind of thing to be loved is contained in the two commandments.
There are four objects of love: God, self, neighbor, and one's body.
No separate commandment is given for love of self and body, since it is contained in love of neighbor.
Self-love and love of one's body come by a law of nature.
